clue.text: Syringe applied to unpleasant growth on the bottom

parts.note: a hypo is a hypodermic syringe
synonym

explanation.surface: A doctor injects something into an ugly lump on a patient's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth on the bottom' sounds medical, but it is botany: extra growth on the underside of a leaf or petal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyponasty is the botanical term for stronger growth on the lower surface of an organ, which makes it curl upwards.

clue.text: Announce summer finally has departed, as weavers do?

definitions.note: a verb phrase: heald as a verb means to thread warp through the heddles

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it, which is the one to go
something that has departed has left, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to herald is to announce
the tail letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone declares that summer has at last gone, as weavers do at season's end.
explanation.walkthrough: HERALD loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A heald is a heddle on a loom, and to heald is to draw the warp threads through them, as weavers do.

clue.text: Name of substance once proposed for your old-fashioned Liberal

parts.note: pro means in favour of
thy is the archaic form of your
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A chemist recalls the name once suggested for a substance favoured by an old Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Prothyl, or protyle, was the hypothetical primordial matter from which all elements were once proposed to derive.

clue.text: Organised lunch gratis for women dancing

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A free lunch has been laid on for the dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautch girls were professional dancing women in India, performing the nautch dance.

clue.text: Performance-enhancing drug supporting female farm worker in Canterbury

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the drug comes below and after the female

parts.note: a female pronoun
EPO is erythropoietin, a banned blood-boosting drug

explanation.surface: A woman on a farm turns to a doping drug to get through the work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the drug under the female. Canterbury is the New Zealand region, not the Kent city.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand a sheepo is the shed hand who keeps the shearers supplied with sheep.

clue.text: Cries from Lowlands pasture rising over local waters

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass
lochs are Scottish lakes

explanation.surface: Shouts echo over the Scottish lochs from the meadows of the Lowlands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above. 'Local' is the Scots flavour: lochs are the waters of Scotland, where the cries come from too.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelloch is Scots for a shrill yell or scream, so the plural fits Lowland cries.

clue.text: Blast from Frenchman after old woman remains in distillery

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
zut is a mild French curse, like 'blast!'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman swears as an old woman lingers at a whisky distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the French oath behind the old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazut is the heavy residue left after petroleum is distilled, used as a fuel oil.

clue.text: Son of PC

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Gaelic surname prefix

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a policeman's boy; a PC is also a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac in Scottish and Irish surnames means son of, and an Apple Mac is a personal computer.

clue.text: Unknown measure reformed vast assemblies

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters of the next word are reordered

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
an em is a printer's measure
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An unspecified step overhauled huge gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Zemstvos were elected local councils in tsarist Russia, and zemstva is the Russian plural.

clue.text: Tie man's worn — wearing dinner jacket, that would be preferable

indicators.note: something worn is battered out of its first shape, so the letters are jumbled
wearing means having clothing on, so the jacket goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tux is a tuxedo
these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's tie is worn with a dinner jacket, which would be the better choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; TIE MAN, jumbled, goes inside TUX.
explanation.definitionFit: Tant mieux is French for 'so much the better', expressing that something is preferable.

clue.text: Point well away from satellite rigged up alone

indicators.note: something rigged has been fixed or tampered with, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satellite dish has been rigged up by one person, far from anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The satellite is the Moon, our natural satellite, not a broadcasting one.
explanation.definitionFit: The apolune is the point in an orbit around the Moon that lies farthest from it.

clue.text: Engine-driver's deep sleep breaking endless hunger

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the word for hunger is dropped
something breaking into a word splits it open and sits inside

parts.note: to long is to hunger; it loses its final letter
a coma is a deep unconsciousness

explanation.surface: A train driver falls into a deep sleep that ends his ravenous hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Locoman is an informal term for a railway worker who drives locomotives.

clue.text: How slow should you march at the back?

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the tail letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A drill instructor asks how slowly a soldier at the rear of the column should march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How slow' reads like a question about pace; here it is an exclamation at someone's dimness.
explanation.definitionFit: Duh is the scornful exclamation meaning 'how stupid can you be', slow here meaning dim-witted.

clue.text: Compound having better reduced part to perform earlier in the day

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so the word for part loses its last letter

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
a role is an actor's part, shortened
synonym
a.m. means before noon

explanation.surface: An actor with a better, shorter part gets to perform in the morning session.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprolactam is an organic chemical compound used to make nylon.

clue.text: Unusual birth of male unsatisfactory, years after arrival

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival
male pronoun
not OK
y is short for year

explanation.surface: A disappointing male birth happened years after the expected due date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After arrival' puts the other pieces behind ARR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrhenotoky is parthenogenesis in which unfertilised eggs develop only into males, as in bees.

clue.text: Reportedly elevated member's spheres of influence

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a raised limb, spoken

explanation.surface: A politician of high rank is said to have spread their spheres of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated member' looks like a senior politician; it is a raised leg.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology a hyleg is the ruling planet or place in a nativity, held to govern a person's life.

clue.text: As French writer's hardly understood at first, leaves that for his compatriots

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters
to leave is to go
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A French author is barely understood at first, so he leaves his writing to fellow Frenchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: His compatriots are the French, so 'that' is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugoesque means in the style of Victor Hugo, the French novelist and poet.

clue.text: Form of servitude, left for days in active retirement?

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands in where the other was

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
d is the abbreviation for day or days
the third age is the active years after retiring

explanation.surface: A pensioner asks whether busy retirement, where weekdays are left behind, is just another kind of servitude.
explanation.walkthrough: THIRD AGE has its D swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirlage was a Scottish feudal obligation binding tenants to grind their corn at a particular mill.

clue.text: Straining to contain Pole letting off steam

indicators.note: to contain means to hold something within, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: straining through a sieve is sifting
N for the north pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man is straining to hold in his anger, then blowing his top.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person; it is a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Snifting describes the valve on a steam engine that releases air or steam from the cylinder.

clue.text: Rushing disastrously into reflective Tavener adagio

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the run is read from right to left
into says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone rushes headlong into a thoughtful slow movement by the composer John Tavener.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gadarene swine of the Gospels rushed down a steep slope into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadarene describes a headlong, reckless rush to ruin, after the possessed herd of pigs.

clue.text: Chemical product: did dash upset fish?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means knocked over, so the word runs bottom to top

parts.note: to dash is to speed; did dash is sped
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A lab worker asks whether hurrying off disturbed the fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A depside is an ester formed from two or more phenolic acids, a substance made by chemical reaction.

clue.text: Loud buzzers made of beryllium alloy, black inside

parts.note: Be is the chemical symbol

indicators.note: inside places the colour's letter within the word for alloy

parts.note: an alloy is a mix of metals
B for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Noisy alarm buzzers are built from a beryllium alloy with something black at the core.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzzers are insects, not alarms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bembix is a genus of sand wasps, known for the loud hum they make in flight.

clue.text: Who would be landed with extra rand to go round?

definitions.text: Who would be landed with extra rand to go round?

indicators.note: to go round means to encircle, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: in cricket a bye is an extra run
to land a prize is to win it
R is the symbol for the South African rand

explanation.surface: A landless farmhand wonders who would gain land if there were more money to share.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a landless South African tenant who would own land, given more money all round. A bye is a run in cricket not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bywoner in South Africa is a poor white tenant farmer living on another's land, someone who would like to be landed.

clue.text: Godwit allegedly from Norfolk once turned up in central Yugoslavia

indicators.note: in places the verb's letters inside the selected pair
central picks the middle letters of the word after it

parts.note: the two letters at the centre of ten
to turn up is to come or arrive

explanation.surface: A bird said to come from Norfolk was once spotted in the middle of Yugoslavia.
explanation.walkthrough: Yugoslavia has ten letters, so its centre is two letters wide. 'Allegedly' marks a disputed meaning: Shakespeare's 'scamels' in The Tempest are uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamel, a word from The Tempest, is sometimes explained as a Norfolk name for the bar-tailed godwit.

clue.text: Ultimately vast scope of tax changes applying retrospectively

indicators.note: changes means the letters before it are altered into a new order
ultimately means in the end, pointing to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the end of the word
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A sweeping set of tax changes is to be backdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex post facto is Latin for 'from after the deed', used of laws that act on earlier events.

clue.text: China to Glamorgan, Washington state to California?

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for Washington
the United States, a state in the sense of a nation

explanation.surface: A traveller lists journeys: China to Wales, Washington State down to California.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang (china plate, mate); Glamorgan is a county in South Wales. The closing 'to California?' is a surface flourish, taking the Washington–state pair down the US coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Wus is a South Wales dialect term of address meaning mate or pal, the Welsh counterpart of china.

clue.text: Provider of poor tips in Kent, perhaps betting on weight

definitions.text: Provider of poor tips in Kent, perhaps

parts.note: SP is the starting price in betting
re means on or concerning
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A racing tipster in Kent gives bad advice by betting on a horse's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' sounds like betting advice. 'Perhaps' warns that the definition is playful rather than a dictionary gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprew is a dialect word whose sense the setter frames as something that spoils tips, with Kent as one regional home.

clue.text: Writer, excellent producer of material for alternative soap

definitions.text: producer of material for alternative soap

parts.note: a quill pen is a writer
A1 means excellent, written as AI

explanation.surface: A fine writer is also a scriptwriter for an alternative TV soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests a TV drama, but it is literal soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The quillai, or soapbark tree of Chile, has bark rich in saponin that is used in place of soap.

clue.text: No longer talking up failure, in brief

indicators.note: in brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a loss is a failure

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped boasting about a short-lived flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Los is an archaic word for praise or renown, so using it was once a way of extolling someone.

clue.text: Emoji of lynx I try, now and again, to represent legendary striker

indicators.note: now and again means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of this run

explanation.surface: Someone tries now and then to depict a famous footballer with a lynx emoji.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer; it is a weapon that strikes, from Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mjolnir is the hammer of the Norse god Thor, which never missed its target.

clue.text: Forces to drink, employing ecstasy and dope

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into drinking alongside drugs and dope.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope sounds like drugs, but it is used in its sense of inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: To enew, in old falconry, is to drive a bird into water, hence to plunge or force into drink.

clue.text: Associate Charlie with swell clothing for figure scary in places!

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the word for swell goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to swell is to grow
an ally is an associate
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A friend called Charlie dresses up in swanky clothes to look frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' marks the answer as regional dialect; the figure is meant to scare birds, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallycrow is a dialect word for a scarecrow, the figure set up in fields to frighten off birds.
